raw_intent:
not just inference, it will be traded anything, we are building a telegraph like network, but we are going to use with KEP to sell projects too

https://docs.telegraphprotocol.com/docs
explicit: CyberAlchemy Exchange is a standalone product and Telegraph-like trading network
Trade scope extends beyond inference to anything the network can support
Use KEP to sell projects too
Project purchases grant KEP co-ownership of the selected exact project/artifact version; existing co-owners remain.
Seller/provider participation is permissionless: no per-participant operator approval; applicable protocol rules still apply.
User says decryption should be the acknowledgement, and requests a design; no separate manual acknowledgement is desired.
Buyer funds escrow before delivery. Unlock commits the purchase for verified recoverable access, with no separate acknowledgement button.
If the deadline passes before unlock commitment, cancel the trade and refund the buyer. After commitment, interrupted delivery is retried; missing client acknowledgement does not cancel the purchase.
Exchange itself operates the trusted service that holds recipient-encrypted key envelopes before purchase commitment and releases them afterward with recovery access.
KEP is part of CyberAlchemy Exchange, not a separate product/project to integrate. Preserve KEP existing encryption and key-handling model.

proposed_interpretation.purpose: A network where people and agents publish, discover and transact offerings, with type-specific fulfillment and evidence. Inference and KEP-mediated project exchange are initial concrete use cases.
proposed_interpretation.standalone: Independent product; exact repository and distribution boundary remains open.
proposed_interpretation.ownership: User owns Exchange product direction; existing KEP product-local definitions retain their meaning.

inherited_distinctions.operator: Operates a network node/service or engine; provider/seller and buyer roles must be modeled separately, even when one identity fills several roles.
inherited_distinctions.caller: Requests inference through the public service contract.
inherited_distinctions.tenant: Existing authorization and request-isolation boundary; final standalone packaging scope remains to be confirmed.

questions.question: What does a project buyer receive: licensed access/copy, KEP non-exclusive co-ownership, exclusive rights, or commissioned work?
questions.boundary: Selection of fulfillment meaning; no payment, license, exclusive transfer, resale or royalty rule inferred.

questions.question: Is initial provider/node participation curated, federated among approved operators, or permissionless?
questions.boundary: Applies to seller/provider participation as asked. Validator/node admission, consensus, verification, settlement and dispute rules remain unselected.

questions.question: What initial pricing, payment, acceptance/dispute and settlement model should Exchange support?
Own repository and installable distribution in the first release?
For project sales, is signed receipt of decryptable delivery sufficient for settlement, or must the project also pass agreed checks?
questions.answer: Buyer-signed delivery/decryption acknowledgement for the exact project version
questions.boundary: Historical answer; current commercial release and cancellation conditions are owned by decryption-settlement-coupling. Escrow-before-delivery and no mandatory quality/build checks remain selected.

questions.question: For project sales, should payment be escrowed before delivery and released on acknowledgement, paid upfront, or requested after acknowledgement?
questions.answer: Escrow before delivery; release after valid signed acknowledgement
questions.boundary: Historical answer; current commercial release and cancellation conditions are owned by decryption-settlement-coupling. Escrow-before-delivery and no mandatory quality/build checks remain selected.

questions.question: What happens when the buyer misses the agreed acknowledgement deadline?
questions.boundary: Historical answer; current commercial release and cancellation conditions are owned by decryption-settlement-coupling. Escrow-before-delivery and no mandatory quality/build checks remain selected.

questions.question: What refund execution/fee rules apply, and how is the grant sequenced so an expired uncommitted purchase adds no membership?
questions.blocks: Cancellation settlement and project fulfillment lifecycle
questions.boundary: Refund on precommit timeout is accepted. No revocation of existing KEP memberships or decrypted knowledge is inferred.

questions.question: Accept proposed verified-access commitment as commercial settlement, with local decryption receipt recorded separately and cancellation only before commitment?
questions.raw_intent: but the decryption should be the acknowledgement
questions.boundary: Accepts clarified product behavior only. A UI click alone is not durable commitment. No selection of release-service trust, proof scheme, payment asset, ledger or implementation is inferred.
questions.answer: Unlock completes the purchase and provides recoverable access. Before commitment, deadline expiry cancels and refunds. After commitment, delivery can be retried and the purchase stays valid; no separate acknowledgement button.

questions.question: Who holds and releases the encrypted key envelope: an initially trusted service or a decentralized mechanism?
questions.answer: Exchange itself is the trusted envelope holding and release service
questions.boundary: Selects envelope custody and release operator. Does not select custody of plaintext/content keys, a correctness verification scheme, ledger, payment asset or deployment. Permissionless seller/provider participation remains selected.

questions.question: Is KEP a separate project with a new encryption/custody model, or the existing protocol inside Exchange?
questions.raw_answer: it remains the same as KEP, KEP is part of the exchange not a separated project
questions.answer: KEP is internal to Exchange; its existing model remains unchanged
questions.boundary: No new server plaintext/content-key custody or separate cryptographic proof system selected. Runtime consistency and adversarial input checks remain implementation responsibilities, not presumed guarantees.

later_questions: Define what a project package contains and its exact version identity
Select initial supported offering types; keep the network model extensible
Define validator/node participation independently from permissionless seller/provider entry.
Define cancellation consequences if access was delivered before acknowledgement; decrypted knowledge is not assumed retractable.
Bind Exchange purchase lifecycle to its internal KEP operations using existing definitions; verify actual implementation behavior.
allowed_use: Clarify product intent and prepare a candidate Definition Pack after answers.
blocked_claims: Canonical KEP renaming or definition promotion
Existing inference tests prove a functioning trading network
Any specific chain, token, federation or payment implementation selected
